name: Overseas-person lawful RMB income — purchase + remittance
when: You are a 境外个人 (passport holder) with lawful China-source RMB income (salary, labour, royalties, etc.).
pros: No annual purchase cap in the rule text for this route (Art. 59); tax/source evidence is the gate, not a quota.
Single documented wire; BOC/HSBC sender fees are small and capped (see costs).
cons: Requires genuine income + tax records; bank reviews authenticity (Art. 68).
Cannot be used for unrelated savings — relabelling principal as salary is prohibited.
steps: Confirm your bank classifies you as 境外个人 (passport) and will accept the income category.
Gather: passport, employment/labour contract, payroll records, China IIT payment records (Art. 59 requires tax vouchers).
At the bank: apply to purchase FX against the income, then remit to your own overseas account (Art. 65: ID only for existing FX).
Keep purchase slip, SWIFT copy and tax records; reconcile U.S. reporting (FBAR/8938, worldwide income).

name: Existing FX remittance (FX already held)
when: You already hold USD/FX in a China FX account (e.g. prior lawful purchase, remittance received).
pros: Overseas-person FX remittance needs only ID (Art. 65) — no purchase quota involved.
No conversion spread if already in USD.
cons: Does not solve the CNY-conversion problem; only helps if FX is already held.
Account identity (境内/境外) still controls; bank may still review source.
steps: Confirm FX balance is in an FX account under your own name.
Instruct remittance to your own overseas account; 境内个人 over USD50,000/day needs transaction evidence (Art. 64).
Retain remittance receipt for U.S. reporting reconciliation.

name: 境内个人 annual facilitation quota (USD50,000/yr)
status: Lawful only if classified 境内个人
when: You are classified 境内个人 (Chinese citizen holding a resident ID) — normally NOT a U.S. citizen with a U.S. passport.
pros: Within quota: ID only, no transaction evidence (Arts. 54–55).
Simple bank purchase + remittance.
cons: A U.S. citizen holding a U.S. passport is 境外个人 under Art. 37 — this quota route does not apply.
Splitting across people/years to evade limits is prohibited (Art. 7; Art. 62 watchlist).
steps: Confirm classification with the bank first — do not assume it.
If 境内个人: purchase within USD50,000/yr, remit; over quota needs transaction evidence (Art. 56).
Never borrow another person's quota.

name: Return of unused prior conversion
when: You previously converted FX to RMB and did not use the RMB.
pros: Direct return path (Art. 14) with ID; no new purchase needed.
cons: Only covers the unused converted amount; needs original exchange slip within 24 months (Art. 60).
steps: Bring passport + original exchange slip.
Apply at bank for return conversion and remittance.

name: Wise from-CNY transfer
when: Non-mainland person with China work history and China tax records within the last 3 years; destination must be your own account.
pros: Designed for exactly this profile; own-account rule keeps it compliant.
Per-transfer caps are clear: CNY300,000 (bank app) / CNY50,000 (Alipay).
cons: Overall limit = after-tax China salary — cannot move unrelated principal.
Fee is quote-time only; no 40-point schedule verified — cost cells stay blank.
steps: Verify identity + tax records with Wise (1–2 working days first time).
Start transfer from China bank app or Alipay; confirm remaining overall limit covers the amount.
Destination must be your own overseas account/Wise account.

name: Bank telegraphic transfer (BOC / HSBC China)
when: Any lawful entitlement (M01, M07–M11) executed as a bank wire.
pros: Published capped sender fees (BOC max CNY410 all-in sender; HSBC max CNY620).
SWIFT record; full-arrival option available (BOC note 5: USD15/25).
cons: Rail only — does not create entitlement; bank still reviews the underlying transaction.
Intermediary/receiving charges excluded from tariff; FX execution rate is the real variable.
steps: Present entitlement documents to the bank (see the entitlement method's steps).
Choose SHA/BEN/OUR charge option; consider full-arrival if intermediary deductions are a concern.
Confirm the executed FX rate and all deductions on the receipt.

name: Emigrant property transfer
when: You have emigrated / are emigrating and transfer pre-emigration property abroad.
pros: The only general capital-account exit for personal property; own-account remittance.
2014 reform: no mandatory staged releases — one or multiple remittances within approval.
cons: Requires emigration status + approval by the original household-registration SAFE office.
Evidence-heavy (identity, hukou, property, tax); approval timelines apply.
steps: Apply to SAFE at original hukou location with identity/property/tax evidence.
Obtain approval; remit to your own overseas account within the approved amount (one or multiple times).

name: Inheritance property transfer
when: You inherit China property/funds as a 境外个人 heir.
pros: Capital-account entitlement; 2014 reform allows combined applications across estates.
cons: Needs notarised entitlement + tax/document review; bank/SAFE approval required.
Inheritance-guide wording inconsistencies flagged (F11) — confirm locally.
steps: Collect death/relationship/entitlement documents and tax records.
Apply for approval; remit to your own account.

name: Sale of China property (境外个人)
when: You actually sell China property held for own use.
pros: Sale proceeds are an approved capital-account exit (Art. 22).
cons: Needs a real sale, IIT on net gain (Art. 6(5)), registration and bank review.
No generic tax rate inferred — basis/proceeds records control.
steps: Complete a genuine sale; pay/evidence IIT on net gain; register transfer.
Apply for SAFE approval to purchase FX and remit proceeds.

name: Insurance proceeds
when: You receive lawful insurance proceeds in China.
pros: May use the overseas-person lawful-income process with policy + insurer payment proof.
cons: Needs genuine policy/proceeds; bank reviews authenticity.
steps: Gather policy and insurer payment proof.
Apply via the M01 income process.

name: Genuine trade / service settlement
when: You have real export/service income with contracts, invoices and customs/tax records.
pros: Current-account settlement for real transactions; no personal quota involved.
cons: Cannot be used to relabel personal savings — fictitious trade is prohibited (Arts. 7, 47).
Bank reviews transaction documents; service payments over USD50,000 need tax filing records.
steps: Maintain genuine contracts/invoices/customs records.
Settle through the bank with transaction documents.

name: Bank draft / cashier's order
when: Same entitlement as M06, executed as a draft instead of a wire.
pros: BOC draft tariff is identical to TT (item 210105008).
Useful where wire rails are unavailable.
cons: Slower; overseas charges still apply; same entitlement review.
steps: Present entitlement documents; request draft issuance at the same tariff as TT (item 210105008).
Mail or present the draft per the bank's instructions; confirm overseas charges and delivery time before issuing.

name: Overseas ATM cash withdrawal (China card)
status: Lawful but capped — not a bulk exit
when: Small amounts only; you hold a China bank card and travel abroad.
pros: No conversion decision needed at the China bank; cash in hand.
cons: SAFE caps: CNY100,000/person/year and CNY10,000/card/day; suspension beyond annual cap.
BOC tariff (12 + 1%, max CNY112) plus possible overseas surcharge; card network/issuer limits also apply.
steps: Withdraw within CNY10,000/day and CNY100,000/year across all your cards.
Never use another person's card (prohibited).
Declare cash over USD10,000 entering the U.S. (FinCEN 105) — see flag F08.

name: Physical cash carry + customs declaration
status: Lawful but capped — not a bulk exit
when: Small amounts only; you travel with cash.
pros: No bank FX spread on carried cash.
cons: Carry limits, customs declaration and U.S. declaration rules apply; permits needed above thresholds.
Not scalable to USD100,000+; security/AML scrutiny.
steps: Check carry limits and permit requirements before travel.
Declare on both sides as required; keep declarations.

name: Underground bank / hawala / informal settlement
pros: None claimed.
cons: Illegal FX settlement; administrative fines and possible criminal liability; funds at risk.

name: Quota splitting / nominee quotas
pros: None claimed.
cons: Art. 7 prohibits splitting to evade limits; Art. 62 watchlist (3-year enhanced review); fines under FX Regulation.

name: Falsified trade / invoices
pros: None claimed.
cons: False commercial documents to evade authenticity review; fines, account closure, criminal referral.

name: Virtual-currency / stablecoin bridge
pros: None claimed.
cons: PBC 2026 No. 42: mainland virtual-currency exchange business strictly prohibited; 2021 notice repealed and replaced.

name: Sham asset sale / gift relabelling
pros: None claimed.
cons: Creating a fake sale/gift to move unrelated principal misstates the transaction; tax and FX penalties.

name: Structuring around bank review thresholds
pros: None claimed.
cons: Deliberately splitting to avoid review is the Art. 7 violation pattern; watchlist and fines apply.
